title: Parse-friendly chunk boundary protocol + sanitized escape policy for streamed structured outputs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a small, parse-friendly framing extension and an escape-normalization policy to make streamed JSON outputs robust across truncation, retries, and non-streaming client compatibility. This ticket defines the framing bytes and metadata we append to each chunk, the canonical escape normalization rules for control characters and partial Unicode sequences, the retry semantics for tool/function calls in the middle of a stream, and a compatibility mode for legacy clients that expect pure LDJSON lines without sentinel framing.
acceptance_criteria: Each stream chunk emitted by the runtime includes an optional single-line chunk header that identifies: chunk_id, parent_message_id, offset_bytes, and an optional checksum. Header is ASCII-safe and terminated with '\n' so existing LDJSON consumers ignore it if present.

An escape-normalization pass guarantees that partial UTF-8 sequences and control characters are encoded using a stable JSON escape form (\uXXXX or "\u{...}") so parsers never receive raw broken sequences.

When a client disconnects mid-object, the server can emit a terminal 'incomplete' chunk containing 'repair_hint' metadata (small canonical suffix) that allows a client to attempt deterministic reconstruction of the last JSON object with at least 90% heuristic success on our test corpus.

Retrying requests with identical idempotency keys results in idempotent tool/function call behavior. If a tool call was in-flight when truncated, the runtime either returns the tool result once (de-duped) or returns an explicit 'duplicate_tool_call' field in the re-stream so clients can detect replay.
Backward compatibility mode: a flag per-route that strips the chunk header and emits plain LDJSON lines; tests that validate both modes run in CI.
Performance impact is measured and documented: additional per-chunk overhead < 2% p99 latency for typical 512-token responses and increase in token bytes < 0.5% on average.
technical_notes: Rationale: many downstream consumers parse by streaming JSON tokenizers that fail on raw truncated UTF-8 or when chunks split strings mid-codepoint. A small header plus canonical escapes reduces parser complexity and improves repairability.

Header format proposal: '#CHUNK <hex(chunk_id)> <hex(parent_id)> <offset> <hex(checksum)>' terminated by LF. Parsers that don't expect '#' treat as LDJSON comment or can ignore if compatibility mode enabled.

Escape normalization: implement a single canonical serializer for outbound characters: control chars (0x00-0x1F) => \u00XX, lone surrogates and broken UTF-8 => \uFFFD \uXXXX fallback sequence. Avoid custom delimiters inside JSON payload so tools/toolcalls remain compatible.

Tool/function call semantics: introduce 'tool_call_checkpoint' metadata in the stream. Checkpoint must be persisted with idempotency key in the request context; replays consult this checkpoint to decide whether to re-run or return cached result.
Security: ensure headers do not leak sensitive IDs. parent_message_id is an opaque hex derived from request UUID truncated to 64 bits. Checksum uses CRC32 to avoid cryptographic overhead.
Compatibility: default behavior for existing routes remains unchanged; new behavior gated by route config 'framing: enhanced' or 'framing: ldjson'.
Open questions: exact encoding for repair_hint (raw bytes vs base64), whether to include full KV cache snapshot pointer in header for high-throughput use cases.
implementation_plan: 1) Add chunk header generator to runtime emitter; make header optional via route config. (ENG change)
2) Add canonical serializer for escape normalization in token->byte pipeline. Integrate with compilation for quantized models to avoid adding CPU path regressions. (runtime/serialization)
3) Persist tool_call_checkpoint in the request transaction log and expose small API to check-and-return cached tool outputs. (orchestration + policy)
4) Add 'incomplete' terminal chunk emission on graceful/abrupt connection close. Implement repair_hint population logic and attach checksum. (stream manager)
5) Add compatibility mode switch and e2e tests that run client sanitizers parsing both legacy and enhanced modes. (test infra)
6) Instrument metrics: chunk_header_bytes, repair_hint_emitted, toolcall_replay_count, parse_error_rate_downstream. (observability)
7) Run canary on a single regional shard for 48h and collect p99 latency and error signals before rollout. (infra + SRE)
8) Publish docs and SDK helpers (JS/Python) that strip header or parse enhanced framing. (DX)
9) Follow-up: consider rolling header into binary protocol for websocket transport.
test_plan: Unit tests for header encoder/decoder: fuzz with random offsets and truncated headers.
Serializer tests: validate that all control chars and malformed UTF sequences are emitted as stable escapes and roundtrip when consumed by our parser shim.
Integration: simulate mid-object disconnects and assert repair_hint allows deterministic repair in at least 90% cases across our test prompt set.
Idempotency: simulate duplicate requests with identical idempotency keys while a tool call is in-flight; assert de-dup or explicit 'duplicate_tool_call' flag returned.
Backwards-compatibility: run legacy client parser against enhanced stream with header present and assert no parse failures for clients configured in compatibility mode.
Performance: microbench p99 latency baseline vs enhanced framing for 256/512/1024 token replies.
Chaos tests: abrupt network drops and replay window expiry tests to validate no silent duplication of external effects.
